newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina sees record 96/97 grain crop 56.3 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Argentina sees record 96/97 grain crop 56.3 mln T.

text.p: Argentina said Wednesday it expects a record crop of 56.3 million tonnes of grain in 1996/97, up from 43.6 million tonnes in 1995/96.
Food Under Secretary Felix Cirio told reporters that the soybean output is expected to reach 13.7 million tonnes, compared with 12.4 million tonnes in the previous year.

Maize production is expected to reach 14.6 million tonnes in 1996/97, versus 10.5 million tonnes a season earlier, whereas output of sunflower seed is expected to be 5.6 million tonnes, up from 5.4 million tonnes.
Cirio said the government was keeping its forecast for wheat output at about 15.2 million tonnes, the same figure it predicted in December and up from 9.2 million tonnes in 1995/96.

Cirio said that total grain output should easily surpass the previous record of 45.8 million tonnes set in 1994/85: "If these estimates are confirmed, it would be an absolute record and by a long way."

Production of wheat, soybeans and maize are all heading for record levels, along with minor crops like peanuts and beans, Cirio said. Cotton and sunflower seed output should be close to all-time highs.

Cirio said higher Argentine farm output was the result of both higher yields due to investment in equipment and agricultural chemicals and also a steady increase in cultivated area, at a record 25.5 million hectares in 1996/97.
"This is not an isolated increase in area, but it confirms a tendency that has been around since the beginning of the 1990s," he said.

Argentine consumption of fertilizer and farm equipment has boomed since the government of President Carlos Menem reduced import tariffs for supplies and scrapped a system of export taxes on agricultural taxes.

Cirio said Argentine ports were coping well with the greater output. They handled 1.7 million tonnes of wheat in December, up from a previous record for the month of 900,000 tonnes. Ports have handled 1.4 million tonnes so far in January, compared to a record of 1.7 million tonnes for the whole month.
